title: A Federated Artificial Intelligence Framework for Optimizing Pancreatic Cancer Treatment - Strategy Update
abstract: arXiv:2609.24718v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While a centralized approach involving patient consent to collect and analyze data centrally would theoretically offer the best data quality and predictive performance, it is not always feasible in practice. Federated Learning (FL) architectures have shown to be a very promising approach to use and access distributed disease related resources within the GDPR boundaries. In a previous case report, we described the preconditions at the participating sites and necessary administrative and process related steps to prepare data, people and infrastructure for improving subtype identification and assessing treatment options in pancreatic cancer. We update this report sharing our experience in tackling the challenges and show preliminary results of the actual federated learning AI pipelines. translated_abstract: 虽然集中式方法（即获得患者同意后集中收集和分析数据）在理论上能够提供最佳的数据质量和预测性能，但在实践中并不总是可行。联邦学习（FL）架构已被证明是一种非常有前景的方法，可以在GDPR（通用数据保护条例）的合规边界内使用和访问分布式的疾病相关资源。在之前的案例报告中，我们描述了参与站点的前提条件，以及为改善胰腺癌亚型识别和评估治疗方案而准备数据、人员和基础设施所需的行政和流程相关步骤。本次我们更新了该报告，分享了我们应对相关挑战的经验，并展示了实际联邦学习AI流程的初步结果。在各参与站点，我们需要识别并标注在本地FL中心完成提取和转换后可访问的数据——在我们的案例中是一个
tldr: 本文更新了此前关于胰腺癌联邦学习框架的案例报告，分享了在GDPR合规约束下多站点协作应对数据、人员和基础设施挑战的实践经验，并展示了联邦学习AI流程在胰腺癌亚型识别与治疗方案评估中的初步结果。
en_tdlr: This paper updates a previous case report on a federated learning framework for pancreatic cancer, sharing practical experience in tackling multi-site challenges on data, personnel, and infrastructure under GDPR constraints, and presenting preliminary results of federated AI pipelines for subtype identification and treatment assessment.
